ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD$ is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$, and $CE$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ADC$. If $\angle BAD = \angle ECD$ and $\angle B = 70^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle CAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Since $AD$ is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$,
\[\therefore \angle ADB=\angle ADC=90^\circ\]

Since $\angle B=70^\circ$,
\[\therefore \angle BAD=20^\circ\]

Since CE is the bisector of $\triangle ADC$,
\[\therefore \angle ECD=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACD\]

Since $\angle BAD=\angle ECD=20^\circ$,
\[\therefore \angle ACD=40^\circ\]

Therefore, in $\triangle ACD$, $\angle CAD=90^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{50^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, B, D, C are on the same straight-line base, A is above D, and AD goes from A perpendicular to the base BC; E is located on AD, and line segment CE connects from C to E on AD, located inside triangle ADC. The figure also shows AB and AC forming two sides of triangle ABC. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, AD is the altitude of triangle ABC, so AD ⟂ BC; therefore ∠ADB = 90°, and because D and C are on BC, ∠ADC = 90°. In right triangle ABD, ∠B = 70°, so ∠BAD = 180° - 90° - 70° = 20°. It is also known that ∠BAD = ∠ECD, therefore ∠ECD = 20°. CE is the angle bisector of ∠ACD in triangle ADC, so ∠ACD = 2 × ∠ECD = 40°. In right triangle ACD, ∠CAD = 180° - 90° - 40° = 50°.
